paragraphs.text: Shipment OJI-10-01 occurred at Ojinaga on 2010-09-11. A former laboratory worker reported secondhand on a load of cannabis that crossed the river near Ojinaga in a pickup truck with a false bed. The source did not know who organized the load, described the crew as local ranch hands working for cash, and could not connect the run to any of the networks that operate in the state. The reporting office treats the account as an example of the small-scale independent smuggling that is constant along this stretch of the border.

The source described conditions in the Ojinaga district as quiet, with the municipal police rarely leaving the town center and ranch roads largely unpatrolled. The source stated that local crews pay a fee to whoever controls the crossing but could not say who that was at the time. The source added that loads of this size are considered beneath the attention of the larger networks. The source added that the pickup trucks used for these runs are bought at auction in the state capital, registered to ranch workers, and abandoned after two or three crossings. The source estimated that such crews cross on most nights when the river is low and that the municipal police are aware of the pattern.

The reporting office assesses this reporting as background on the crossing environment. The source's access is historical and secondhand. This reporting is consistent with the pattern of activity observed on the corridor in prior months. The account is retained because it may help establish a baseline for the volume of independent traffic at the crossing.
